ingredients: 15 g kombu (dried kelp), about a 10 cm square
steps: Wipe the kombu lightly with a damp cloth, keeping the white powder, and soak it in the cold water in a pot for 30 minutes.
Heat over medium-low and remove the kombu just before the water boils, when tiny bubbles form at the edge (about 60-70 C).
Bring to a boil, add a splash of cold water, then scatter in the katsuobushi and turn off the heat.
Let the flakes sink for 2-3 minutes, then strain through a cloth-lined sieve without squeezing; this ichiban dashi keeps 3 days chilled.

ingredients: 150 g silken or soft tofu, cut in 1.5 cm cubes
steps: Soak the wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain and squeeze.
Heat the dashi to a simmer over medium heat and add the tofu cubes for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to low, place the miso in a ladle or strainer and dissolve it into the stock with chopsticks.
Add the wakame and heat until just steaming; do not let it boil after the miso goes in.
Ladle into lacquer bowls and top with spring onion; serve with rice and pickles.

ingredients: 200 g thinly sliced pork belly, cut in 4 cm pieces
150 g daikon radish, cut in thin quarter-moons
1 medium carrot, cut in thin half-moons
80 g gobo (burdock root), shaved; or parsnip
150 g konnyaku, torn in small pieces and parboiled
2 spring onions, sliced, and shichimi togarashi to serve
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and stir-fry the pork until it changes colour, about 2 minutes.
Add the daikon, carrot, gobo and konnyaku and stir for 2 minutes to coat in the fat.
Pour in the dashi, bring to a boil, skim off the scum and simmer for 15 minutes until the daikon is tender.
Add the tofu, lower the heat and dissolve the miso into the soup without boiling.
Serve topped with spring onion and a shake of shichimi.

ingredients: 8 small raw prawns, peeled and deveined; or 120 g white fish
4 sprigs mitsuba (Japanese parsley); or flat-leaf parsley
steps: Season the dashi with salt, light soy sauce and sake and bring to a gentle simmer.
Poach the prawns in a little of the seasoned dashi for 2 minutes until pink and opaque throughout.
Arrange prawns, kamaboko and a knotted mitsuba sprig in each covered soup bowl.
Pour the hot clear stock gently over, add a twist of yuzu peel and serve covered at once.

ingredients: 1 litre kombu-shiitake dashi (10 g kombu and 4 dried shiitake soaked 30 minutes in water)
150 g daikon, cut in thin quarter-moons
80 g gobo (burdock root), shaved; or parsnip
2 satoimo (taro), peeled and sliced; or small potato
2 tbsp usukuchi soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin, 1/2 tsp salt
steps: Slice the soaked shiitake and keep the strained kombu-shiitake liquid as the stock.
Heat the sesame oil over medium heat, stir-fry the root vegetables, konnyaku and shiitake for 3 minutes, then crumble in the tofu by hand and fry 2 minutes more.
Add the dashi, bring to a boil, skim, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the taro is tender.
Season with soy sauce, mirin and salt, simmer 2 minutes and serve this Zen temple soup hot.

ingredients: 300 g chicken thigh, cut in bite-size pieces
1 small carrot, sliced into flower shapes
100 g komatsuna or spinach, blanched and cut in 4 cm lengths
2 tbsp usukuchi soy sauce, 1 tbsp sake, 1/2 tsp salt
4 strips yuzu peel and mitsuba to garnish
steps: Bring the dashi to a boil, add the chicken and carrot, skim and simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Season with soy sauce, sake and salt.
Meanwhile grill or toast the mochi for 6-8 minutes until puffed and golden.
Place a mochi in each bowl with the greens and kamaboko, pour the hot soup over and garnish with yuzu and mitsuba; serve on New Year's morning and warn diners to take small bites of the sticky mochi.

ingredients: 450 g (3 rice-cooker cups) Japanese short-grain rice (uruchimai), e.g. Koshihikari; or Calrose
1 piece (5 cm) kombu, optional, for a subtle savoury note
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl, swirling gently and pouring off the cloudy water 4-5 times until it runs almost clear.
Drain and soak the rice in the measured water in a heavy pot for 30 minutes.
Cover, bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 13 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes to steam, then fluff with a wet paddle (shamoji) and serve in rice bowls.

ingredients: 600 g freshly steamed Japanese short-grain rice, still warm
80 g canned tuna, drained, mixed with 1 tbsp Japanese mayonnaise
steps: Wet your hands with water and rub them with a pinch of salt.
Take about 75 g of rice, make a dent in the centre and add a teaspoon of one filling.
Close the rice over the filling and press firmly 3-4 times into a triangle with cupped hands.
Wrap each triangle with a strip of nori just before eating so it stays crisp; keep fish-filled onigiri cool and eat the same day.

ingredients: 400 ml hot sencha or hojicha tea, or hot dashi
1/2 sheet nori, cut in thin strips
steps: Grill the salted salmon under a medium-hot grill for 8-10 minutes until cooked through, then flake it, removing skin and bones.
Put the rice in two bowls and top with the salmon, sesame, nori and a dab of wasabi.
Pour the hot tea around the rice and serve at once, scattering over arare for crunch.

ingredients: 450 g Japanese short-grain rice, rinsed and drained
150 g chicken thigh, cut in 1 cm dice
2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sake, 1 tbsp mirin, 1/2 tsp salt
Mitsuba or spring onion to garnish
steps: Soak the rinsed rice in the dashi for 30 minutes in a heavy pot or rice cooker.
Stir in the soy sauce, sake, mirin and salt, then lay the chicken, mushrooms, vegetables and aburaage on top without stirring.
Cover, bring to a boil, then cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and chicken cooked through.

Drain the rice (keep the liquid), mix with the beans and steam in a cloth-lined steamer over high heat for 40 minutes, sprinkling with the red liquid every 10 minutes.
Mix the sesame with the salt and sprinkle over the pink rice; serve for birthdays and celebrations.

ingredients: 200 g hot freshly steamed Japanese rice
1 very fresh egg (use pasteurised eggs outside Japan)
1 tsp soy sauce (or TKG soy sauce)
1 pinch katsuobushi-free furikake or toasted sesame
steps: Put the hot rice in a bowl and make a well in the centre.
Crack the egg into the well, add the soy sauce and whisk with chopsticks into the rice until fluffy and pale yellow.
Top with spring onion and sesame and eat straight away.

ingredients: 250 g boneless chicken thigh, cut in 2 cm pieces
2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp sugar
Mitsuba or spring onion to garnish
steps: Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a simmer in a small frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and chicken and simmer for 6-7 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through.
Pour two-thirds of the egg over, cover for 30 seconds, then add the rest and cook until just set but still soft.
Slide over bowls of hot rice and garnish with mitsuba.

ingredients: 250 g very thinly sliced beef (shoulder or short plate)
3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake, 1 tbsp sugar
Beni shoga (red pickled ginger) to serve
steps: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and ginger in a pan over medium heat, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.

Spoon the beef, onion and some sauce over bowls of rice and top with beni shoga; a raw or soft-boiled egg is a common addition.

ingredients: 2 pork loin cutlets (120 g each), pounded to 1 cm
30 g plain flour, 1 egg for coating, 50 g panko breadcrumbs
120 ml dashi, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp sugar
steps: Season the pork, dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg and press into panko.
Deep-fry at 170 C for 5-6 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through (71 C inside); drain and slice into strips.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sugar and onion in a small pan for 4 minutes, lay a sliced cutlet on top and pour half the beaten egg around it.

ingredients: 6 large prawns, peeled with tails on, deveined
1 small Japanese eggplant (nasu) and 4 slices kabocha squash
100 g cake flour or plain flour, 1 egg yolk, 180 ml ice-cold water
60 ml soy sauce, 60 ml mirin, 1 tbsp sugar, 60 ml dashi for tare
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and dashi for 3 minutes until slightly syrupy to make the tendon sauce.
Score the underside of the prawns so they stay straight and pat everything dry.
Mix the egg yolk and ice water, add the flour and stir only a few strokes, leaving lumps.
Dip pieces in batter and fry at 175 C for 2-3 minutes until pale gold and crisp, prawns cooked through; drain on a rack.
Arrange the tempura over rice in bowls and drizzle with the warm sauce.

ingredients: 4 tbsp ketchup, plus extra to serve
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a frying pan over medium heat, fry the onion 2 minutes and the chicken 5 minutes until cooked through.
Add the rice and ketchup, season, and fry until evenly red and hot; divide between two plates, shaping into ovals.
Beat 2 eggs with 1 tbsp milk, melt half the remaining butter in a small pan and scramble the eggs briefly, then let them set into a soft, glossy omelette.
Slide the omelette over the rice, tuck the edges with paper towel and repeat; finish with a ribbon of ketchup or demi-glace.

ingredients: 400 g chicken thigh or beef chuck, cut in bite-size pieces
100 g Japanese curry roux blocks (e.g. Vermont or Golden Curry)
800 g hot steamed Japanese rice and fukujinzuke pickles to serve
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the meat for 4 minutes, then add the onions and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the carrots, potatoes and water, bring to a boil, skim and simmer covered for 20 minutes until tender (longer, about 60 minutes, for beef).

Simmer on low for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy; serve beside rice with fukujinzuke or rakkyo.

Soy sauce and gari (pickled ginger) to serve

Place a half nori sheet, shiny side down, on a bamboo mat and spread a thin layer of rice over it, leaving 1 cm bare at the far edge.
Dab a line of wasabi and lay a stick of tuna (tekkamaki) or cucumber (kappamaki) along the centre.
Roll tightly with the mat, press to square it, and cut each roll into 6 pieces with a wet knife; serve with soy sauce and gari, using only sashimi-grade fish kept well chilled.

1 thick tamagoyaki omelette, cut in long strips
8 kanpyo (dried gourd strips), simmered in soy sauce and sugar
4 dried shiitake, soaked and simmered in soy sauce, mirin and sugar, sliced
4 tbsp sakura denbu (sweet pink fish flakes) or 4 crab sticks
1 Japanese cucumber, cut in long strips
steps: Place a full nori sheet on a bamboo mat and spread 150 g rice evenly over it, leaving 2 cm bare at the far edge.
Lay the egg, kanpyo, shiitake, spinach, cucumber and denbu in neat lines across the centre.
Roll the mat over firmly in one motion so the fillings stay centred, press and seal.

4 dried shiitake, simmered in soy sauce, mirin and sugar, sliced
1 small carrot, cut in matchsticks and simmered in dashi
60 g snow peas, blanched and sliced
2 tbsp ikura (salmon roe) and nori strips to top
steps: Fold the shiitake and carrot into the seasoned rice and spread it in a shallow lacquer box or platter.
Scatter the shredded egg evenly over the rice like a yellow blanket.
Arrange the sashimi, prawns and snow peas on top, then dot with ikura and nori.
Serve within an hour, keeping it cool; use only sashimi-grade fish bought the same day.

3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp mirin
400 g sushi rice seasoned with sushi-zu

Simmer the pouches in the kombu dashi, soy sauce, sugar and mirin under a drop lid on low heat for 15 minutes until most liquid is absorbed; cool.
Mix the sesame and chopped ginger into the sushi rice and form into 12 small balls.

ingredients: 150 g sashimi-grade yellowtail (hamachi) or sea bream (tai)
150 g daikon, cut in very fine threads (tsuma) and soaked in iced water
2 tsp freshly grated wasabi or wasabi paste
steps: Buy only sashimi-grade fish from a trusted fishmonger the same day and keep it below 4 C until serving.
Pat the fish dry and, with a very sharp knife (yanagiba), slice across the grain in single long pulling strokes into 1 cm thick slices.

Lean the slices against the daikon in overlapping rows, add a mound of wasabi and serve at once with small dishes of soy sauce.

ingredients: 12 large prawns, peeled with tails on, deveined
1 Japanese eggplant, 1 small sweet potato and 8 slices kabocha squash
150 g cake flour or plain flour, plus extra for dusting
1 egg yolk and 240 ml ice-cold sparkling water
Neutral oil with a little sesame oil for frying
200 ml dashi, 50 ml soy sauce, 50 ml mirin (tentsuyu)
100 g daikon, grated, and 1 tsp grated ginger

Dust each piece in flour, dip in batter and fry in small batches at 170-180 C for 1-3 minutes until pale gold and crisp, prawns cooked through.

ingredients: 4 pork loin chops (150 g each), 2 cm thick, fat edge snipped
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
Tonkatsu sauce, karashi mustard and lemon wedges to serve
steps: Season the pork, coat in flour, dip in egg and press firmly into panko on both sides.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry two chops at a time for 6-7 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and 71 C in the centre.
Drain on a rack for 3 minutes, then slice into strips.
Serve on a mound of shredded cabbage with tonkatsu sauce, mustard, rice and miso soup.

1 tsp grated ginger and 1 clove garlic, grated
Lemon wedges and Japanese mayonnaise to serve

Drain off excess marinade and toss the pieces in the mixed potato starch and flour.

ingredients: 600 g floury potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp sugar
Neutral oil for frying; tonkatsu sauce and shredded cabbage to serve
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender, drain, dry over low heat and mash roughly.
Fry the onion in butter over medium heat for 3 minutes, add the mince and cook 5 minutes until browned and cooked through; season with salt, pepper and sugar.
Mix the meat into the potato, cool, and shape into 8 oval patties.
Coat in flour, egg and panko, then deep-fry at 180 C for 2-3 minutes until golden; serve with tonkatsu sauce and cabbage.

ingredients: 4 boneless chicken thighs, skin on (about 600 g)
steps: Prick the chicken skin with a fork and season lightly with salt.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the chicken skin side down for 7-8 minutes until crisp and golden, then turn and cook 4-5 minutes until cooked through.
Wipe out the excess fat, add the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar and simmer, spooning over, for 2-3 minutes until the sauce is glossy and coats the meat.
Slice and serve over rice with the sauce, with a little shredded cabbage on the side.

ingredients: 500 g thinly sliced pork loin or shoulder
steps: Mix the ginger, soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar and marinate the pork for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat and fry the onion for 2 minutes until softened.
Add the pork in a single layer, cook 1-2 minutes per side until no longer pink, then pour in the remaining marinade and toss until it glazes the meat.
Serve with shredded cabbage, rice and miso soup.

ingredients: 2 mackerel (saba) fillets, about 150 g each, skin on
steps: Pat the mackerel dry, sprinkle both sides with sake and salt and rest for 20 minutes, then pat off the moisture.
Score the skin twice and grill skin side up under a hot grill or on a fish grill for 10-12 minutes until the skin is blistered and the flesh flakes and is opaque throughout.
Serve with a mound of grated daikon dressed with soy sauce, a lemon wedge, rice and miso soup.

ingredients: 400 g yellowtail (buri) collar or fillet, cut in large pieces
600 g daikon, peeled, cut in 3 cm rounds
1 thumb (20 g) ginger, sliced, plus shreds to garnish
steps: Parboil the daikon rounds in water for 15 minutes until a skewer goes in with some resistance; drain.
Pour boiling water over the fish, then rinse in cold water to remove blood and scales.
Put daikon, fish, ginger, water and sake in a pan, bring to a boil, skim and add the sugar, mirin and soy sauce.
Simmer under a drop lid on low heat for 30 minutes, basting, until the daikon is amber and tender and the fish cooked through; serve garnished with ginger shreds.

ingredients: 250 g thinly sliced beef (or pork in eastern Japan)
4 potatoes, peeled and cut in large chunks
4 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake, 2 tbsp sugar
1 tbsp neutral oil and a few snow peas to garnish
steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and stir-fry the beef until it changes colour, then add the onion, potato and carrot and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the dashi, sake, sugar and mirin, bring to a boil and skim.
Add the shirataki and soy sauce, cover with a drop lid and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes to absorb flavour, then serve garnished with blanched snow peas.

ingredients: 500 g mixed minced beef and pork (aibiki)
1 onion, finely chopped and sauteed until golden, cooled
30 g panko soaked in 3 tbsp milk
1/2 tsp salt, pinch pepper and nutmeg
3 tbsp ketchup, 3 tbsp tonkatsu or Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp red wine or water
steps: Knead the mince with salt until sticky, then mix in the onion, soaked panko, egg, pepper and nutmeg.
Shape into 4 oval patties, slapping between your palms to remove air, and press a dent in the centre.
Fry in oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until browned, turn, add 3 tbsp water, cover and cook on low for 8 minutes until the juices run clear (71 C inside).
Remove the patties, add the ketchup, sauce and wine to the pan juices and simmer 1 minute, then spoon over; serve with rice and salad.

ingredients: 600 g very thinly sliced well-marbled beef
1 piece beef suet or 1 tbsp oil
2 negi (Japanese leeks), cut diagonally, and 200 g shungiku (chrysanthemum greens) or spinach
100 ml soy sauce, 100 ml mirin, 50 ml sake, 3 tbsp sugar, 100 ml water (warishita)
4 very fresh eggs for dipping (pasteurised outside Japan)
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and water briefly to make warishita.
Heat a cast-iron sukiyaki pan at the table and rub with suet, then sear a few beef slices, sprinkle with a little sugar and splash with warishita.
Add the tofu, shirataki, mushrooms and leeks in sections, pour in more warishita and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add more beef and the greens as you eat, cooking the beef until no longer pink, and dip each bite in beaten egg; serve with rice.

ingredients: 600 g paper-thin sliced beef or pork
1.5 litres water with a 15 cm piece kombu, soaked 30 minutes
150 ml ponzu sauce with grated daikon and spring onion
steps: Heat the kombu water in a donabe or hot pot at the table and remove the kombu just before it boils.
Add the vegetables, mushrooms and tofu to the simmering broth and cook 5 minutes.
Each diner swishes a slice of meat through the simmering broth ("shabu-shabu") for 10-20 seconds until no longer pink, pork until fully cooked.
Dip in ponzu or sesame sauce; skim the broth as you go and finish with udon or rice cooked in it.

ingredients: 3 tbsp usukuchi soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp sake, 1 tsp salt
500 g daikon, cut in 3 cm rounds and parboiled
300 g assorted fish cakes (chikuwa, hanpen, satsuma-age, gobo-maki)
200 g konnyaku, cut in triangles and parboiled
1 block atsuage (thick fried tofu), cut in pieces
steps: Season the dashi with soy sauce, mirin, sake and salt in a large pot.
Add the daikon, eggs, konnyaku and kombu knots and simmer very gently, without boiling, for 1 hour.
Pour boiling water over the fish cakes and atsuage to remove oil, add to the pot and simmer 20-30 minutes more.

ingredients: 600 g boneless chicken thigh, cut in 3 cm pieces
2 negi (Japanese leeks), cut in 3 cm lengths
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar for 10 minutes until reduced by a third to make tare.
Thread the chicken and leek alternately onto skewers (negima).
Grill over hot charcoal or under a hot grill for 8-10 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Brush with tare 2-3 times in the last minutes, or season with salt only (shio), and serve with shichimi and cold drinks.

ingredients: 150 g napa cabbage, finely chopped, salted and squeezed
1 tsp grated ginger and 1 clove garlic, grated
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sake, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1/2 tsp salt
1 tbsp neutral oil and 100 ml water for frying
Soy sauce, rice vinegar and rayu (chilli oil) for dipping
steps: Mix the pork, cabbage, chives, ginger, garlic and seasonings until sticky.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edge and pleat one side to seal into a crescent.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat, arrange the gyoza flat side down and fry 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden.

steps: Beat the eggs gently with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce and mirin without making foam.

ingredients: 1 tsp usukuchi soy sauce, 1 tsp mirin, 1/2 tsp salt
80 g chicken thigh, diced small, sprinkled with soy sauce
4 slices kamaboko and 4 ginkgo nuts or shiitake slices
steps: Beat the eggs gently, mix with the dashi and seasonings, and strain through a fine sieve.

ingredients: 1 block (400 g) silken or soft tofu, pressed 20 minutes
80 g daikon, grated, and 1 tsp grated ginger
1 spring onion, sliced, and a pinch of katsuobushi
steps: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce and mirin for 1 minute to make the sauce and keep warm.
Cut the tofu into 8 cubes, pat dry and coat thinly in potato starch.
Fry at 170 C for 3-4 minutes until pale golden and crisp.
Place in bowls, pour the warm sauce around and top with daikon, ginger, spring onion and katsuobushi.

steps: Drain the tofu and cut it into 2 square pieces on chilled plates.
Top with spring onion, ginger, shiso and sesame (omit the usual bonito flakes to keep it vegetarian).
Drizzle with soy sauce just before serving on a hot summer day.

ingredients: 400 g frozen or fresh edamame in pods
1 tbsp coarse salt, plus 1 tsp to finish
steps: Rub fresh pods with 1 tbsp salt to remove fuzz and brighten the colour (skip for frozen).
Boil the water and cook the edamame for 3-5 minutes until the beans are tender but still bright green.

ingredients: 300 g salted salmon (shiozake) or cod, in chunks, including bones
steps: Soak kombu in the water for 20 minutes, then heat to just below a boil and remove it.
Blanch the salted fish in boiling water 30 seconds to remove scum and excess salt.
Add daikon, carrot and potato to the broth and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add fish and sake and simmer 8 minutes until the fish is cooked through, then add leek, check salt and serve hot.

ingredients: 300 g salmon (or venison), cut in chunks
50 g wild garlic (kitopiro/gyoja ninniku) or garlic chives
1 tbsp fish oil or vegetable oil
steps: Simmer the kombu in water for 10 minutes to make a light broth, then remove it.
Add daikon, potato and carrot and cook 15 minutes until tender.
Add the salmon and simmer 8 minutes until opaque and cooked through.
Season with salt and a little oil, stir in the chopped kitopiro for the last minute and serve this simple Ainu soup hot.

ingredients: 1 kg king crab (tarabagani) legs, cooked or raw, cut into sections
2 tbsp light soy sauce (usukuchi) and 1 tsp salt
steps: Bring dashi, sake, mirin, soy and salt to a simmer in a donabe.
Add cabbage stems, leek and mushrooms and simmer 5 minutes.

ingredients: lemon wedges and rice vinegar, to serve
steps: Bring the water and salt (seawater strength) to a rolling boil in a large pot.

Drain and cool on its back so the kani-miso (tomalley) stays inside.
Crack the legs, open the shell and eat the sweet meat with the kani-miso as a sauce, with lemon or vinegar.

ingredients: 1 large hokke no hiraki (butterflied, semi-dried Atka mackerel), about 400 g
steps: Heat a fish grill or broiler to high and oil the rack.
Grill the fish flesh-side to the heat first for 7-8 minutes until golden, then skin-side 4-5 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Squeeze moisture from the grated daikon and pile beside the fish with a drop of soy sauce.
Serve with lemon, rice and miso soup, flaking the juicy flesh away from the bones.

ingredients: 2 pork loin cutlets (120 g each), pounded thin
50 g flour, 1 egg and 60 g panko, for coating
steps: Melt butter in a pan, fry the bamboo shoots 2 minutes, then add rice, ketchup and salt and stir-fry until hot and evenly coloured.
Coat the pork in flour, egg and panko and fry at 170C for 5-6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Warm the demi-glace sauce.
Mound the rice on plates, lay the sliced cutlet on top, pour over the demi-glace and serve with cabbage.

ingredients: 4 Hokkaido potatoes (danshaku or May Queen), about 200 g each
steps: Steam the unpeeled potatoes over boiling water for 30-40 minutes until a skewer slides in easily.
Cut a deep cross on top of each and squeeze the base to open it up.
Put a thick slice of butter in each, sprinkle with salt and pepper and serve hot as the butter melts in.

steps: Boil the potatoes 15 minutes until soft, drain, mash smooth while hot and knead in the potato starch and salt.
Shape into 8 discs about 1.5 cm thick.
Fry in oil and butter over medium heat 3 minutes per side until golden and chewy.
Add soy sauce, sugar, mirin and water and turn the cakes until coated in a glossy sweet-salty glaze.

ingredients: 160 g tuna-mayonnaise salad (canned tuna mixed with mayonnaise)
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt and milk, knead 10 minutes, add butter and knead until smooth and elastic, then let rise 60 minutes until doubled.
Fill each chikuwa with tuna-mayonnaise.
Divide dough into 8, roll each into a rectangle, wrap around a stuffed chikuwa and seal; proof 30 minutes.
Brush with egg and bake at 190C for 12-15 minutes until golden, in the style of Sapporo's Donguri bakery.

steps: Heat milk, sugar, milk powder and cornstarch over medium heat, stirring, until just simmering and slightly thickened, about 8 minutes.
Cool, stir in cream and vanilla and chill at least 4 hours.
Churn in an ice-cream machine until thick and soft-serve consistency, about 20 minutes.
Pipe in tall swirls onto cones at once, while still soft and milky.

ingredients: 4 kiritanpo sticks (pounded rice grilled on cedar skewers), cut diagonally
300 g Hinai jidori chicken thigh (or free-range chicken), bite-size
steps: If making kiritanpo, half-pound 400 g warm rice, press around wooden skewers and grill until golden, then slice.
Bring the stock, soy sauce, sake and mirin to a simmer, add chicken and burdock and cook 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add maitake, leek and shirataki and simmer 5 minutes.

steps: Pound the hot rice with a pestle until half-crushed and sticky, mixing in the salt.

Grill over charcoal or under a broiler 8-10 minutes, turning, until golden and crusty.
Mix miso, sugar, mirin and sesame, brush over the kiritanpo and grill 1-2 minutes more until the miso bubbles and toasts.

ingredients: 600 g beef tongue, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
600 ml oxtail soup with spring onions
nanban miso pickles or Chinese cabbage pickles, to serve
steps: Score the tongue slices lightly and rub with salt, pepper, sake and sesame oil, then rest in the fridge overnight.
Grill over hot charcoal or a very hot grill pan 2 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through but still juicy.
Slice into strips if large.
Serve as a Sendai set with barley rice, oxtail soup and pickles.

steps: Simmer soy sauce, sake, mirin, sugar and water, add the salmon and poach 6-8 minutes until cooked through, then remove.

Briefly dip the ikura into the warm liquid (10 seconds) so it turns pale, then drain.
Flake the salmon over the cooked rice in bowls and spoon the ikura on top, as served on the Watari coast of Miyagi.

ingredients: 400 g white fish fillet (cod, pollock or flounder), skinless and boneless
soy sauce and grated ginger, to serve
steps: Blend the fish to a very smooth paste, add salt and knead until sticky, then blend in egg white, starch, sugar and mirin.
With oiled hands shape into bamboo-leaf (sasa) shapes about 1 cm thick.
Grill on an oiled pan or grill over medium heat 3-4 minutes per side until puffed, golden and cooked through.
Serve warm or cool with ginger and soy sauce, a Sendai specialty.

steps: Buy only live, sashimi-grade hoya from a trusted fishmonger and prepare the same day.
Cut off both nozzles, slit the shell and pull out the orange flesh, removing the dark gut and rinsing in salted water.
Slice the flesh into bite-size pieces and chill on ice.
Serve with cucumber and a dip of vinegar, soy sauce and ginger; its sweet-salty-bitter flavour pairs with local sake.

ingredients: 300 g edamame in pods (or 150 g shelled)
steps: Boil edamame in salted water 5 minutes, drain, pod and rub off the thin inner skins.
Mash or pulse to a coarse paste with sugar, salt and 2 tbsp water.
Knead shiratamako with water into a soft dough, roll into small balls and boil 3 minutes after they float, then plunge in cold water.
Drain and coat generously with the green zunda paste, as served in Sendai.

ingredients: 2 tbsp grated daikon and 2 tbsp sliced spring onion
2 tbsp ikura or tuna sashimi and nori, as condiments
steps: Simmer dashi, soy sauce, mirin and chicken 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked, keeping the broth hot.
Cook the soba 4 minutes until tender, rinse in cold water and portion into many tiny mouthfuls.
Dip each portion briefly in the hot broth and drop into the diner's small bowl.
Keep refilling as fast as they eat until they cover the bowl with its lid; serve the condiments alongside, Morioka style.

ingredients: 2 portions reimen noodles (chewy wheat and potato starch noodles)
800 ml cold beef stock, fat skimmed
2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp salt
1 tbsp rice vinegar and 1 tsp sugar
seasonal fruit such as watermelon or nashi pear
steps: Season the beef stock with soy sauce, salt, vinegar and sugar and chill until ice-cold.
Boil the noodles 1 minute, then rub and rinse in iced water until firm and chewy.
Place noodles in chilled bowls and pour over the cold soup.
Top with beef, egg, cucumber, kimchi and fruit, adding kimchi to taste for heat.

ingredients: 1 tsp each garlic and ginger, grated
steps: Fry the pork, garlic and ginger in sesame oil until cooked, then stir in miso, sesame paste, sugar and 4 tbsp water and cook 5 minutes into a thick meat miso.
Boil the noodles until tender and drain without rinsing.
Top noodles with meat miso, cucumber and spring onion and mix well with vinegar, chili oil and garlic to taste.
Leave a little in the bowl, crack in the egg, add hot noodle water and miso, stir and drink as chitantan soup.

ingredients: 3 tbsp black or white sesame seeds
steps: Mix flour, salt, baking powder, water and oil into a firm dough and rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 16 balls, press each flat to about 2 mm and press sesame seeds onto one side.
Cook in a hot, heavy pan pressed with a weight (or a senbei iron) over medium heat 2-3 minutes per side until crisp and pale golden, with thin crunchy edges.
Cool on a rack to crisp fully; eat as a snack or keep for senbei-jiru.

ingredients: 6 soup-type Nanbu senbei (or crisp wheat crackers), broken in pieces
4 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp mirin
steps: Simmer dashi with chicken, burdock and carrot 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add shiitake, cabbage, leek, soy sauce and mirin and simmer 5 minutes.
Drop in the senbei pieces and cook 2-3 minutes until they turn chewy like dumplings but keep some bite, then serve.

ingredients: 1 l clear fish or kombu dashi
steps: Heat the dashi with sake, salt and soy to a gentle simmer.
Add the abalone and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the uni lobes and poach 1 minute until just firm; they look like wild strawberries (ichigo) floating in the soup.
Ladle into lacquer bowls and garnish with shiso; this Hachinohe soup is served at celebrations.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g warabi or zenmai (mountain vegetables), chopped
steps: Simmer all the diced vegetables, aburaage, konnyaku and soybeans in the dashi 30 minutes until very tender.
Dissolve the miso into the broth and heat 5 minutes without boiling.
Serve hot; this Tsugaru (Aomori) dish is made in a large pot for Little New Year and reheated over several days.

ingredients: 1 cod head and bones with some flesh (about 600 g), cut in pieces
steps: Sprinkle the cod pieces with salt, rest 10 minutes, then pour boiling water over and rinse to remove scum.
Simmer kombu water, daikon and carrot 10 minutes, then add the cod and simmer 10 minutes until fully cooked.
Dissolve the miso, add the leek and simmer 2 minutes.
Serve this Aomori winter soup piping hot, sucking the rich meat from the bones.

ingredients: 2 large scallop shells (hotate), cleaned, with 4 scallops
steps: Set a large scallop shell over a direct flame or charcoal grill as a pan.
Pour in dashi, add the scallops and leek and simmer 3 minutes, then dissolve the miso.
Pour in the beaten egg and cook 1-2 minutes until just set and the scallops are opaque.
Sprinkle with spring onion and eat straight from the shell with rice, Aomori style.

ingredients: 200 g dried Inaniwa udon (thin hand-stretched udon)
1 tsp grated ginger and 1 spring onion, sliced
steps: Simmer dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar 2 minutes, then chill to make the dipping sauce.
Cook the udon in plenty of boiling water 3-4 minutes until silky and tender.
Rinse in cold running water, then chill in iced water until glossy and firm.
Serve cold with the dipping sauce, ginger, spring onion and sesame.

steps: Smoke the whole daikon over smouldering hardwood (cherry or oak) in a smoker or covered grill for several hours, or buy ready-smoked daikon, until wrinkled and smoky.
Mix rice bran, salt, sugar, sake lees and kombu to make a pickling bed.
Pack the daikon in the bran in a container, weight it and leave to pickle in a cool place for at least 2-4 weeks.
Rinse, slice thinly and serve with rice or with cream cheese; ready-made iburigakko from Akita is a good substitute.

ingredients: 4 tbsp shottsuru (Akita fish sauce) or Thai fish sauce

Add the hatahata and simmer gently 8 minutes until cooked through.
Add seri for the last minute and serve from the pot at the table.

ingredients: 300 g thick straight steamed yakisoba noodles
4 tbsp sweet Worcestershire-style yakisoba sauce mixed with 2 tbsp dashi

steps: Rub the taro with salt and rinse to remove sliminess, then simmer in the water with konnyaku 15 minutes until a skewer goes in.

5 cm piece kombu (gagome or nebari kombu), finely chopped

Mix all the chopped vegetables, herbs and kombu in a bowl.

Chill 15 minutes and spoon over hot rice or cold tofu.

Put noodles in chilled bowls, pour over the cold soup and add a few ice cubes.
Top with beef, menma and spring onion and serve at once.

ingredients: 500 g ball konnyaku (tama konnyaku), about 20 balls

Thread 3-4 onto skewers and serve with mustard, as at Yamagata temples and festivals.

ingredients: 2 portions thick flat curly ramen noodles (hira-uchi)

ingredients: 1 sheet nori and 1 spring onion, sliced
steps: Heat the clear chicken stock until just simmering.

ingredients: 50 g dried wood ear mushrooms (kikurage), soaked
2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp light soy sauce
steps: Soak the dried scallops in the water overnight to make the broth, then shred them.

Add wood ear and scallops and simmer 5 minutes, then season with salt and soy.
Add the mame-fu for the last 2 minutes and serve in shallow lacquered bowls, as for Aizu celebrations.

ingredients: 2 long thick leeks (negi), with a slight curve
steps: Simmer dashi, soy sauce and mirin 2 minutes and chill or keep warm as the soup.

Place soba in bowls, pour over the soup and top with daikon and katsuobushi.

ingredients: 60 g dried squid (surume), cut in thin strips
steps: Boil sake and mirin 1 minute to cook off alcohol, add soy sauce and sugar and cool.
Mix the squid and carrot strips in a container.

Serve as a side dish with rice or sake, a Fukushima New Year staple.

ingredients: 300 g extra-thick yakisoba noodles (about 3 times usual thickness)
steps: Heat the lard on a hotplate or large pan over high heat and fry the pork until cooked through and crisp.

Add the noodles and sauce and toss 3-4 minutes until the thick noodles are glossy and heated through.
Serve with a sprinkle of ichimi, as made in Namie town.

ingredients: 450 g Japanese short-grain rice (uruchimai), washed until the water runs clear
500 ml water plus a 5 cm piece kombu
80 ml red rice vinegar (akazu) or rice vinegar
400 g mixed sashimi-grade fish (tuna akami, kohada, sea bream), sliced 7 mm thick
2 tsp freshly grated wasabi or wasabi paste
4 tbsp nikiri (2 tbsp soy sauce simmered with 1 tbsp mirin and 1 tbsp sake)
steps: Use only sashimi/sushi-grade fish from a trusted fishmonger; keep it chilled until shaping, and slice it against the grain into neat 7 x 3 cm pieces.
Soak the washed rice with the kombu in the water for 30 minutes, remove the kombu, then cook covered on medium-high until boiling, lower to low for 13 minutes and rest off the heat 10 minutes.
Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved, tip the hot rice into a wide wooden tub (hangiri) and fold the vinegar in with slicing motions while fanning until glossy and body temperature.
With wet, vinegared hands, form 18 g ovals of rice, dab a little wasabi on the underside of each fish slice and press the fish over the rice with two fingers so it hugs the rice gently.
Brush each piece with nikiri, Edo-style, so no extra soy dip is needed, and serve straight away with gari and hot green tea.

steps: Rinse the kanpyo, rub it well with the salt until it softens and turns translucent, then rinse and boil 5 minutes until a fingernail marks it easily.
Simmer the kanpyo in the kombu dashi, soy sauce, sugar and mirin on low heat for 20 minutes until the liquid is almost gone and the strips are glossy brown; cool and cut to nori length.
Lay a half sheet of nori shiny side down on a bamboo mat, spread 150 g rice evenly leaving 1 cm bare at the far edge, and lay kanpyo strips across the centre.
Roll tightly with the mat into a square-ish thin roll, rest it seam-side down 1 minute, then slice with a wet knife into 6 pieces.

ingredients: 100 g squid or small shrimp, chopped
steps: Whisk the flour into the dashi with the Worcestershire and soy sauce until there are no lumps; set the thin batter aside.
Heat a griddle or wide frying pan to medium-high with the oil, add the cabbage, seafood and tenkasu, and stir-fry with two spatulas for 3 minutes until the seafood is opaque and cooked.
Chop the mixture fine and push it into a ring (the "bank"), then pour half the batter into the centre and let it bubble 1 minute before folding everything together and adding the rest of the batter.
Spread it into a thin layer, scatter the mentaiko and cheese, and cook 3–4 minutes until the base crisps and the top is gooey.
Sprinkle with aonori and eat straight off the griddle with small hagashi spatulas, as in Tsukishima.

ingredients: 2 freshwater eels (unagi), about 300 g each, butterflied and boned (or ready-steamed unagi)
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar on low heat for 10 minutes until reduced by a third and syrupy to make the tare; set aside.
Cut each eel into 3–4 pieces and thread on flat metal skewers; grill skin-side to the heat over charcoal or a hot grill for 4 minutes per side until lightly charred.
Kanto-style, steam the grilled eel for 10–15 minutes until very tender and fluffy, then return it to the grill.
Brush with tare and grill 1 minute per side, repeating 3–4 times until lacquered and the flesh flakes easily and is cooked through.
Remove the skewers, sprinkle with sansho, and serve hot with rice and a clear liver soup (kimosui) if you like.

ingredients: 1 prepared unagi kabayaki fillet (about 250 g), fresh or vacuum-packed
4 tbsp unagi tare (soy, mirin, sugar reduced)
30 g Nara-zuke or other Japanese pickles, to serve
steps: Cut the eel into pieces the width of your bowl, sprinkle with the sake and warm in a 200°C oven or under the grill for 5–6 minutes until hot through and sizzling.
Brush the eel with tare and grill 1 more minute until glossy.
Fill two lidded bowls with rice, drizzle each with a spoon of tare, then lay the eel on top and spoon over a little more tare.
Cover for 1 minute so the steam softens the eel, then sprinkle with sansho and serve with pickles.

ingredients: 300 g shelled asari clams (or 800 g clams in shell, purged in salted water)
steps: If using clams in shell, steam them with the sake in a covered pot on high for 3 minutes until opened, discard unopened ones, remove the meat and strain the juice into the dashi.
Bring the dashi to a simmer, add the leek and aburaage and cook 3 minutes until soft.
Dissolve the miso into the broth off the boil, add the clam meat and heat 1 minute only so the clams stay tender.
Spoon rice into bowls and ladle the clam miso soup over it, Fukagawa fishermen's style; finish with shichimi.

ingredients: 60 g small dried fish (chirimen jako) or 100 g fresh asari clam meat
20 g kombu left over from making dashi, cut in 1 cm squares
steps: Put the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and ginger in a small heavy pan and bring to a boil.
Add the kombu and simmer on low for 15 minutes, then add the fish or clam meat.
Keep simmering on the lowest heat, stirring now and then, for 20–25 minutes until the liquid is nearly gone and everything is dark and glossy.
Stir in the sesame, cool, and keep in a jar in the fridge for up to two weeks; serve a spoonful with plain rice.

ingredients: 300 g boneless chicken thigh, cut in chunks
250 g minced chicken mixed with 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 egg and 1 tbsp potato starch (tsukune)
1 small carrot and 150 g daikon, sliced thin
200 g fresh udon, for the finish
steps: Bring the stock, soy sauce, mirin and sake to a simmer in a large clay pot (donabe).
Add the carrot, daikon and chicken thigh and simmer 8 minutes, then drop in spoonfuls of the tsukune mixture and simmer 5 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Add the cabbage, leek, shiitake and tofu and simmer 6–8 minutes until tender.
Eat at the table straight from the pot, as sumo wrestlers in Ryogoku do.
Finish by cooking the udon in the remaining broth for 3 minutes and serving it as the last course.

ingredients: 300 g live or fresh loach (dojo), cleaned (substitute small whole smelt)
2 tbsp Edo amamiso (sweet miso) or white miso
2 bunches naganegi (green leek), sliced thinly into a big pile
steps: Rinse the loach, place in a shallow pan with the sake and simmer covered on low heat for 10 minutes until the bones soften and the fish is cooked through.
Mix the dashi, miso, soy sauce and sugar and pour it over the loach in a shallow iron nabe.
Simmer on a tabletop burner for 8–10 minutes until bubbling and slightly reduced.
Heap the leek on top, let it wilt 1 minute, then season with sansho and eat with rice, as at Asakusa's old dojo restaurants.

ingredients: 300 g horse meat (sakura niku), thinly sliced (substitute thinly sliced lean beef)
3 tbsp Edo amamiso (sweet miso) or awase miso
steps: Stir the miso, dashi, mirin, sugar and soy sauce together to make the warishita.
Arrange the leek, shirataki and tofu in a shallow iron nabe, pour in the warishita and bring to a simmer on a tabletop burner.
Lay the meat slices on top and cook 1–2 minutes, turning, until no longer pink at the edges; cook horse meat through to at least medium.
Lift each piece out and eat with the vegetables, dipped in beaten raw egg Tokyo-style if you like (use pasteurised eggs if concerned), with rice.

ingredients: 300 g fatty tuna (toro or cheaper chutoro scraps), cut in 2 cm cubes
3 naganegi (thick leeks), cut in 4 cm lengths
steps: Grill or pan-sear the leek pieces on medium-high for 4 minutes until charred in spots.

steps: Bring the mirin and sake to a boil for 30 seconds to cook off the alcohol, stir in the soy sauce and cool.
